title: Is a new customer worth it?
principle: Each customer must earn more margin than winning them cost.

screens.text: Let me tell you about PepperTap, an Indian grocery delivery app that started in 2014. It gave big discounts to get buyers. In 2015, it said it got 40,000 orders in one day. In April 2016, it stopped delivering groceries.

screens.prompt: PepperTap had so many orders. Why do you think it stopped delivering groceries?

options.label: Other apps copied its prices and features
It spent too much getting each order
Shops no longer wanted to sell to it

screens.why: Its boss said the company lost cash on every order. Discounts and the high cost of getting new customers used up its money. Orders fell to about 7,000 or 8,000 a day. Then it stopped delivering groceries.

screens.title: LTV:CAC
screens.text: To find what one new customer costs you, divide your total spend by the number of new customers. Spend ₹4,000 to get 10 customers, and each costs ₹400. This is called customer acquisition cost, or CAC. Lifetime value should be much higher than CAC. This comparison is called LTV:CAC.

screens.prompt: You spend ₹3,000 on Instagram ads. The ads bring 10 new families. How much did you spend to get each family?
screens.why: Yes. ₹3,000 ÷ 10 families = ₹300 each. This is your CAC.

wrong.b: You spent ₹3,000 to get all 10 families. Divide by 10, and you get ₹300 per family.

screens.title: Now look at your business
screens.text: Two lessons ago, you saw how to get customers without paying for each one. But paying can work when a customer brings in more than you spend. It's late June. A family that stays usually orders 4 cakes a year. You keep ₹450 from each cake.

screens.prompt: You spend ₹600 to get a new family. Each cake leaves you ₹450. How many cakes must they buy to earn back ₹600?
screens.why: Yes. After one cake, you have ₹450, so you still need ₹150. After two cakes, you have ₹900, which is more than ₹600. This is called payback: the number of orders needed to earn back what you spent to get a customer.

wrong.a: One cake leaves you ₹450, but you spent ₹600. You still need ₹150. After 2 cakes, you have ₹900. So you earn back your cost after 2 cakes.
wrong.c: You earn back the money sooner. After 2 cakes, you have ₹900, more than the ₹600 you spent. So you earn back your cost after 2 cakes.

screens.prompt: I'll show you six ways you got new families last year. For each one, tell me: did you earn back what you spent?

items.text: Spend ₹300 on ads, and the family orders 4 cakes a year
Spend ₹500 on free samples, and the family orders one cake
Put a ₹5 card in a box, and the family orders 4 cakes a year
Pay a blogger ₹2,000, and 2 families order once each
Give ₹100 in referral discounts, and the family orders 4 cakes a year
Give ₹500 off each of 2 cakes, and the family never orders again

screens.why: Good. The ads, the card and the referrals cost less than the families brought in. The free samples, the blogger and the big coupon cost more than the ₹450 you kept from each cake sold.

screens.prompt: Ads cost ₹300 per new family. Each family is worth about ₹9,000 over five years. You have ₹30,000. Why not spend it all?

options.label: You pay now, but the ₹9,000 takes years
You spend too much at ₹300 per family
You cannot use ads after one month

screens.why: Yes. Remember Unit 1: a business can close if it runs out of cash. Each family pays you back slowly, one cake at a time. Spend a little first. Then use the money you earn to pay for more ads.

wrong.b: ₹300 is small compared with ₹9,000. But when do you get the money? Remember Unit 1: you spend ₹30,000 now, but earn ₹9,000 per family over five years. You could run out of cash before then.
wrong.c: We don't know that. The problem is when you get paid. Remember Unit 1: you spend ₹30,000 now, but earn ₹9,000 per family over five years. You could run out of cash before then.

screens.setup: It's the end of June. Your referral offer is still running. You have kept ₹6,000 from profit to get new families, so you have enough cash. A family that stays usually orders 4 cakes a year. You keep ₹450 from each cake.
screens.question: How will you spend the ₹6,000?

options.label: Give every customer ₹300 off any cake
options.outcome: The coupon is used for 20 orders. But 14 are from families who already buy from you. Only 6 families are new. So each new family costs ₹1,000. You keep just ₹150 from each family's first cake.
options.why: Most discounts went to customers you already had. Divide the total cost by only the new families. Your CAC was ₹1,000.
options.better: Pay to show your Instagram reels to more people. Each new family costs about ₹300.

options.label: Spend ₹6,000 to promote Instagram reels
options.outcome: The reels bring 20 new families at ₹300 each. You keep ₹450 from each family's first cake, so you earn back the cost on the first order. If they stay a year, each family brings you ₹1,800 in margin.
options.why: You spend ₹300 to get a family that brings ₹1,800 a year in margin. You earn back the ₹300 on the first cake. The numbers look good.

options.label: Pay a food blogger ₹6,000 for one post
options.outcome: The post looks good and brings 8 new families. Each costs you ₹750 to get. They must buy two cakes for you to earn that money back. But some families buy only once.
options.why: You could still earn back the cost over time. But each family costs more than twice what you paid with reels.
options.better: Pay to show your Instagram reels to more people. Each new family costs about ₹300.

screens.text: Divide what you ___ by the number of new customers. Each customer must bring you more ___ than that.
screens.why: Yes. This is the idea behind LTV:CAC. Your reels brought new families at ₹300 each. Each family brings you ₹1,800 a year in margin.

summary: CAC: total money spent to get new customers ÷ number of new customers gained.
LTV:CAC: lifetime value must be much higher than CAC. Otherwise, getting more customers can make you lose money.
Payback: how many orders a customer must place before you earn back their CAC. If it takes too long, you can run out of cash.

cards.front: You spend ₹6,000 on ads and get 20 new customers. What is the CAC?
You spend ₹500 to get a customer. They order once, leaving ₹200. Was it worth it?
options: Yes, a sale is a sale
cards.back: The margin a customer brings must be more than what you spent to get them.

cards.front: You spend ₹600 to get a customer. Each order leaves ₹300. How many orders to earn back the cost?
cards.back: ₹300 × 2 = ₹600. You earn back the cost on the second order.
